simple: Palo Alto Networks’ line of hardware next-generation firewalls — from PA-500 and PA-1500 for branches to PA-3500 and PA-5500 for campuses and data centers, the modular PA-7500 chassis and the ruggedized PA-50R for industrial sites and transportation. Identifies applications regardless of port and encryption (App-ID), users (User-ID, Cloud Identity Engine) and devices, decrypts TLS including post-quantum algorithms, segments the network and connects offices over IPsec VPN; managed with Panorama or the cloud-based Strata Cloud Manager. On this site we assume the firewall comes with two subscriptions by default. The Precision AI Network Security bundle: Advanced Threat Prevention — an intrusion prevention system (IPS) that blocks exploits, spyware and even unknown command-and-control (C2) channels inline; Advanced WildFire — a cloud sandbox that checks unknown files; Advanced URL Filtering — real-time website analysis that blocks phishing and malicious pages; Advanced DNS Security — blocks dangerous domains, DNS tunnels and malware-generated domains (DGA); Advanced IP Defense — blocks attacker infrastructure by IP; Device Security — discovers and classifies IoT and other unmanaged devices on the network; Advanced SD-WAN. The Prisma Access Agent subscription — an agent for employee remote access through the firewall (it replaces the GlobalProtect gateway license).
